$comment: THE OPERATOR SET INDEX — an ENUMERATION, not a merge.
docs/implementation-artifacts/design-the-compiler-and-the-bands.md section 3 found that
'the operator set' — what a config author's YAML may express — has no single address. It is
held, correctly, across several independently-authored surfaces that agree by TEST, never by a
shared type. This file is that address for the surfaces named below, and ONLY those surfaces.
THIS FILE DOES NOT MERGE THE SURFACES. app/present/qualification.ts:60-68's own comment argues
against widening its type to admit the engine's orderable comparisons; app/present/
declaration.ts:32-54's own header states the federation across readers is deliberate ('one
served document, four strict readers, each owning one axis'). Nothing here is imported BY
qualification.ts, generate-qualification-declaration.mjs, membership.ts or
qualification-agreement.py — each keeps deciding its own grammar. This file is read only by
tests/operator-set-agreement.test.mjs, which probes each surface's ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR and
asserts it matches what is named here — an outside witness, not a shared dependency.
SCOPE — why this indexes TWO vocabularies, not six surfaces.
design-the-compiler-and-the-bands.md section 3.1's own table lists SEVEN files answering FOUR
different kinds of question, not one: what a predicate may TEST (operators), what a predicate
may test it ON (fields), what an edge may be (structural.ts), what an ordering/chrome may be
(resolutiontable.ts), what an output rendition may be (resolution.ts — the table's own row
calls this 'closed to output facts only', a different axis: OUTPUT shown, not INPUT accepted),
and what YAML SYNTAX is even readable before any of the above apply (yaml-subset.mjs, a parse
layer, not a grammar layer). A single index spanning all seven would flatten four different
questions into one shape none of them actually have. This file indexes the two that share a
shape and a purpose — MEMBERSHIP OPERATORS and RESOLVABLE FIELDS — because both answer the one
question 'what may a section's own qualification predicate say about a line being typed', and
because both, uniquely among the seven, turned out (this document's own verification, see
'corrections' below) to be duplicated on BOTH sides of the compile boundary, which is exactly
where an unwitnessed agreement is most expensive to lose. STRUCTURAL, RESOLUTION-TABLE,
RENDITION and YAML-SYNTAX are real closed vocabularies too, each already refusing loudly in its
own file (see the citations design-the-compiler-and-the-bands.md section 3.1 gives for each),
but each answers a different question and none is indexed here. A truthful index over the two
that share a shape beats a strained one over all seven.
CORRECTIONS TO THE REPORT THIS INDEX WAS COMMISSIONED FROM.
1. The brief that commissioned this work, and design-the-compiler-and-the-bands.md's OWN
backlog row (backlog.yaml id 'the-operator-set-has-no-single-address') both list SIX
surfaces and both omit app/present/resolution.ts's RESOLUTION_KEYS (the RENDITION
vocabulary), even though section 3.1's own table documents it as a seventh row with its own
citation. The count 'six' undercounts the design document's own table by one. See the SCOPE
note above for why RENDITION is excluded here regardless — the miscount and the exclusion
are separate findings and this file is explicit that it is only asserting the second.
2. Section 3.2 of the same document states RESOLVABLE_FIELDS 'is exported from a .mjs Node
script and is structurally unreachable from the browser's TypeScript at compile time, so
even that one list cannot be the operator set's address.' THAT IS FACTUALLY WRONG, verified
directly in this worktree: app/present/membership.ts:69 independently declares
'export const RESOLVABLE_FIELDS = ["node_type", "domain", "status"] as const;' — a BROWSER
twin the design document never opened. A THIRD copy lives in
scripts/qualification-agreement.py:62 as TRIPLE_FIELDS, whose own comment ('Kept in step
with RESOLVABLE_FIELDS in scripts/generate-qualification-declaration.mjs and
app/present/membership.ts') proves the author of THAT file already knew about the browser
twin the design document missed. So RESOLVABLE_FIELDS is not one list with no address on one
side — it is THREE independently hand-synchronised lists, none importing from another, which
is a sharper version of the design document's own finding than the design document itself
stated, not a refutation of its thesis.
WHAT WIDENING THIS SET MEANS. Adding a predicate operator (e.g. an orderable comparison) or a
resolvable field is a decision that today requires editing memberOperators / resolvableFields
below AND every one of the surfaces listed, in the same pull request, or
tests/operator-set-agreement.test.mjs goes red naming exactly which surface fell out of step.
RESOLVABLE_FIELDS STOPPED BEING THREE HAND-TYPED COPIES, THEN STOPPED BEING A HAND-TYPED LIST
AT ALL. scripts/generate-qualification-declaration.mjs:96 used to be the one hand-authored
copy; scripts/generate-operator-set.mjs wrote app/present/membership.ts's and scripts/
qualification-agreement.py's copies FROM it. 2026-08-06 (the operator's own diagnosis: 'we have
nodes and fields etc all declared in yaml... that should be compiled and be the source of
truth') retired that constant: scripts/compile-qualification.mjs's deriveResolvableFields(files)
now DERIVES the set from a config's own vocabulary+schema, and generate-operator-set.mjs writes
app/present/membership.ts's copy from compiling the REAL monorepo config. This file was
deliberately NOT made the generation source (see CORRECTIONS above) — it exists to OBSERVE the
surfaces, by test, and handing it a second job as the thing that DEFINES the value would blur
that. This index, and the resolvableFields 'values' list below, remain independently
hand-authored — a snapshot of what the real config compiles to today, checked against the
generated copy, not derived from it.
scripts/qualification-agreement.py's TRIPLE_FIELDS is NO LONGER one of the generated copies —
see scripts/generate-operator-set.mjs's own header, 'WHY qualification-agreement.py IS NO
LONGER A TARGET'. Its whole method (an exhaustive cross product of every axis's value domain)
was tractable at three low-cardinality fields and is not tractable at eighteen; it is now a
DELIBERATELY hand-frozen subset of resolvableFields, asserted (at run time, in that file) to
remain a subset, rather than a copy kept in lockstep with it.

memberOperators.description: The complete set of operator keys a MEMBERSHIP predicate may use, both as the browser reads a served declaration and as the compiler normalises a pattern into one. Anything outside this list must be refused, loudly, by every surface below.

resolvableFields.description: The complete set of node fields a section's own predicate may range over, for a line the operator is typing (not yet an existing node). Anything outside this list is a field the browser cannot resolve locally and the surface must refuse or withhold it. SNAPSHOT, 2026-08-06: what scripts/compile-qualification.mjs's deriveResolvableFields(files) computes against the real monorepo config today (35 node types, 55 distinct schema fields) — a MEASUREMENT, not a design decision independent of the config. 'project' (60 refusals before this change) and 'stage' (6) are the two most-referenced fields that remain OUTSIDE this list: both are set only by a per-section 'defaults:' block (never a vocabulary token, never the global registration default), which the current compiler cannot yet admit safely on every use — see compile-qualification.mjs's own header, section (b)/(c), and this PR's description for the full account.

surfaces.name: RESOLVABLE fields (compiler)
surfaces.symbol: deriveResolvableFields (function, not a literal — see its own header)

surfaces.name: RESOLVABLE fields (browser) — NOT in the six-surface report; found verifying it
surfaces.symbol: RESOLVABLE_FIELDS (generated from deriveResolvableFields against the real config)

surfaces.name: RESOLVABLE fields (python agreement generator) — also NOT in the report; DELIBERATELY a subset, not a copy, since 2026-08-06 — see scripts/generate-operator-set.mjs's header
surfaces.side: compiler (test-fixture generator, run against the engine directly)

excludedSurfaces.name: STRUCTURAL edge vocabulary
excludedSurfaces.reason: Answers 'what may an edge be', a topology question, not what a predicate may test.

excludedSurfaces.name: RESOLUTION table vocabulary
excludedSurfaces.reason: Answers 'how may a section order or draw its rows', a presentation question, not what a predicate may test.

excludedSurfaces.name: RENDITION vocabulary
excludedSurfaces.reason: Closed to OUTPUT facts only (the file's own design citation) — what the app may show two ways, not what config may express as input. The design document's own table lists this as a seventh row; the six-surface report omits it entirely.

excludedSurfaces.name: YAML SYNTAX subset
excludedSurfaces.reason: A parse layer — governs what characters are readable at all, before any predicate or field grammar applies. Orthogonal vocabulary; design-the-compiler-and-the-bands.md section 3.1 itself notes the syntax and predicate refusal lists 'share zero vocabulary items'.
